query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases is governed by the formation of non-protective oxides, particularly Mn-based oxides, which deplete the bulk alloy of Mn and lead to catastrophic failure.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix
generation.intervention: Elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 700-1050 °C, gas environment: oxidizing or reducing
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of non-protective oxides, particularly Mn-based oxides
generation.mechanism: Depletion of Mn from the bulk alloy, leading to degradation and catastrophic failure
generation.predicted_outcome: Catastrophic failure due to degradation of the alloy
generation.baseline: No degradation or failure in the absence of elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 700-1050 °C, gas environment: oxidizing or reducing
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of degradation and the role of other alloying elements in the degradation process are not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: In situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) experiment to investigate the high-temperature oxidation behavior of the alloy
measurements: Oxide formation, Mn depletion, and alloy degradation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no non-protective oxides are formed and no Mn depletion is observed, the hypothesis is falsified
